# Stacklit

> Stacklit writes a small, committable JSON index of a codebase (modules, exports, dependency edges, hints) and a symbol graph, so AI coding agents can orient themselves without re-exploring the repo each session. Free, MIT licensed, one Go binary, deterministic, runs locally with no LLM, and the CLI makes no network calls.

Key facts:
- Install: `npx stacklit init`, `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit`, `npm install -g stacklit`, or `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest`.
- Output: `stacklit.json` (index), a Mermaid dependency file (`DEPENDENCIES.md` by default, `output.mermaid` in `.stacklitrc.json`), `stacklit.html` (interactive map), `stacklit derive` (compact text map for prompts).
- Deterministic: same repo gives the same bytes. Hard token budgets on queries (`--budget`).
- Languages: 48 languages and formats in the index; the symbol graph (query, explain, impact, path, hubs, slice) covers 20 languages.
- Assistants: `stacklit setup` configures 26 targets, including Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, Zed and a generic AGENTS.md. MCP server via `stacklit serve` (stdio, 15 tools, or `--profile minimal` for 4).
- Privacy: no telemetry, no account, no upload. The generated HTML map requests small language logos from thesvg.org unless `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off`. The only opt-in external call is `stacklit init --summary`.
- Benchmarks: reproducible, no LLM calls, three pinned repos. The derived map is 137 to 1,372 tokens. The benchmark does not show a token saving over grep; it shows cheap orientation. Limitations are documented.
- Not a search engine. When the exact identifier is known, grep is cheaper.

Stacklit parses your repo with tree-sitter and writes `stacklit.json`: modules, exports, dependency edges and hints. Commit it, and an agent reads a few hundred tokens instead of rediscovering the layout every session.
Free and MIT, no paid tier. One Go binary, local and deterministic, no LLM, and the CLI makes no network calls. (The map page can load language icons from thesvg.org; `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off` removes that.)

## Install

```bash
npx stacklit init                                   # scan, write the index, open the map
stacklit setup                                      # wire up the assistants it detects
git add stacklit.json && git commit -m "add stacklit index"
```

Also: `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit`, `npm install -g stacklit`, `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest`, or a binary from [Releases](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/releases).

## See it

## Output

`stacklit derive` prints a compact map for a prompt (gin v1.10.0, 137 tokens, module list trimmed here):

```
gin | go | 8 modules | 19,537 lines | Gin, GitHub Actions, net/http
test: go test ./... | env: PORT

modules:
  binding             binding | depends: bytesconv, json
  internal/bytesconv  bytesconv | depended-by: binding, render, root
  render              render | depends: bytesconv, json
  root                root package | depends: binding, bytesconv, json, render
do-not-touch: .github/
```

`stacklit query` returns a token-budgeted slice of the symbol graph (output trimmed here):

```
$ stacklit query "how is the symbol graph built" --budget 600
internal/cli/graphcmds.go
  50-63 func buildSymbolGraph(root string, includeTests ...bool) (*graph.SymGraph, error)
      calls BuildSymbols E0.95
internal/graph/resolve.go
  955-961 func BuildSymbols(root string, files []string, eo ExtractOptions) *SymGraph
```

## What you get

| | |
|---|---|
| Index | `stacklit.json`, a Mermaid diagram (`DEPENDENCIES.md` by default, set with `output.mermaid`) and an interactive `stacklit.html` map |
| Languages | 48 languages and formats indexed; symbol graph for 20 ([list](docs/LANGUAGES.md)) |
| Queries | `query`, `explain`, `impact`, `path`, `hubs`, `slice`, each with a hard `--budget` |
| MCP | `stacklit serve`: 15 tools, or `--profile minimal` for 4 (about 230 tokens of schema) |
| Hooks | git post-commit refresh; optional Claude Code hook that points a grepped identifier to its definition |
| CI | `export` (graphml, cypher, dot, mermaid and more), `check` architecture rules, `status` freshness, `merge-graphs`, a [GitHub Action](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit-action) |
| Deterministic | same repo, same bytes. A committed index only changes when the code does |
| Privacy | no telemetry, no upload. The map loads language logos from thesvg.org unless `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off` ([details](docs/PRIVACY.md)) |

`stacklit setup --list` shows all 26 targets, including Aider, Cline, Continue, OpenCode, Roo Code, Kiro and a generic `AGENTS.md`. Anything else can read `stacklit.json` directly.

## Benchmark

Three pinned repos, 30 navigation tasks, no model calls, tokens as bytes / 4. The index is 2,524 to 16,126 tokens and the derived map 137 to 1,372. This does **not** show a token saving over grep: when the exact symbol is known, grep is cheaper, and the grep and read baseline found the answer on 30 of 30 tasks against 27 for the map path. What it shows is cheap orientation. Method, misses and limits: [bench/RESULTS.md](bench/RESULTS.md).

# Stacklit usage guide

Complete reference for the `stacklit` command line, the MCP server, configuration and the `stacklit.json` format. For a short introduction see the [README](../README.md).

Contents: [Install](#install) | [First run](#first-run) | [Command reference](#command-reference) | [MCP server](#mcp-server) | [Configuration](#configuration) | [Environment variables](#environment-variables) | [Reading stacklit.json](#reading-stacklitjson) | [Monorepos](#monorepo-support) | [Polyrepo scanning](#polyrepo-scanning) | [CI/CD](#cicd) | [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

---

## Install

Pick one:

```bash
npx stacklit init                                              # no install, downloads the binary on first use
npm install -g stacklit                                        # global install
go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest    # from source, needs Go
```

Or download a binary for macOS, Linux or Windows (amd64 and arm64) from [Releases](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit/releases).

Check the install:

```bash
stacklit --version
```

---

## First run

```bash
cd your-project
stacklit init
```

Typical output:

```
[stacklit] found 342 files
[stacklit] parsed 342 files (0 errors)
[stacklit] done in 89ms -- wrote stacklit.json, DEPENDENCIES.md, stacklit.html

Opening visual map...
```

(File counts and timing vary. Go repos index in milliseconds; Python and TypeScript repos can take seconds, see [bench/RESULTS.md](../bench/RESULTS.md).)

Commit the portable outputs. `stacklit.html` is gitignored and regenerates with `stacklit view`.

```bash
git add stacklit.json DEPENDENCIES.md
git commit -m "add stacklit codebase index"
```

Then tell your tools about it, either automatically with `stacklit setup` or by hand:

**Claude Code**, add to `CLAUDE.md`:
```
Read stacklit.json before exploring files. Use modules to locate code, hints for conventions.
```

**Cursor and other MCP clients**, add to the MCP config:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "stacklit": { "command": "stacklit", "args": ["serve"] }
  }
}
```

**Copilot**, add to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:
```
Read stacklit.json first to understand codebase structure before exploring files.
```

**Any other agent**: `stacklit.json` is plain JSON. Point the agent at it.

---

## Command reference

All commands run against the current directory. Run `stacklit <command> --help` for the built-in help.

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| [`init`](#stacklit-init) | First-time scan, write all outputs, open the visual map |
| [`generate`](#stacklit-generate) | Regenerate the outputs from current source |
| [`view`](#stacklit-view) | Rebuild `stacklit.html` from `stacklit.json` and open it |
| [`diff`](#stacklit-diff) | Check whether the index is stale |
| [`derive`](#stacklit-derive) | Print the compact navigation map, or inject it into an agent config file |
| [`export`](#stacklit-export) | Render the index as markdown, or export the graph as GraphML, Cypher, JSON, DOT, Mermaid, an Obsidian vault or a markdown wiki |
| [`setup`](#stacklit-setup) | Configure detected AI tools and install the git hook |
| [`serve`](#stacklit-serve) | Run the MCP server over stdio |
| [`graph`, `query`, `explain`, `impact`, `path`, `hubs`, `communities`, `report`, `slice`, `watch`](#symbol-graph-commands) | Symbol-level graph and token-budgeted queries |
| [`doctor`](#stacklit-doctor) | Diagnose config, hooks, a stale index and parse errors |
| [`ingest`](#stacklit-ingest) | Add docs, OpenAPI, SQL schemas and ownership to `stacklit.context.json` |
| [`check`](#stacklit-check) | Enforce layer boundaries, cycles, fan-in and fan-out limits and orphans (exit code 3 on violation) |
| [`merge-graphs`](#stacklit-merge-graphs) | Merge symbol graphs from several repos and link them by package names |
| `completion` | Shell completions for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell |

Global flags: `--version`, `--help`.

### stacklit init

```
stacklit init [--hook] [--summary] [--multi FILE] [--workspace PATH]
```

Scans the current directory, writes `stacklit.json`, `DEPENDENCIES.md` and `stacklit.html`, then opens the HTML in your default browser.

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--hook` | Install a git `post-commit` hook that runs `stacklit generate --quiet` and stages `stacklit.json` and the configured mermaid file (`DEPENDENCIES.md` by default). An existing hook is appended to, never replaced. (The flag's built-in help text says "pre-commit"; the hook that is installed is `post-commit`.) |
| `--summary` | Add an AI-written architecture narrative to the index. This is the only opt-in feature that sends data anywhere, see [Summary](#summary-opt-in). |
| `--multi FILE` | Polyrepo mode: scan every repo path listed in FILE. See [Polyrepo scanning](#polyrepo-scanning). |
| `--workspace PATH` | Accepted but currently has no effect on the scan. Monorepo workspaces are detected automatically. |

### stacklit generate

```
stacklit generate [--quiet]
```

Same scan and outputs as `init`, without opening a browser. Use this in scripts, hooks and CI.

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--quiet` | Suppress progress output |

### stacklit view

```
stacklit view
```

Reads `stacklit.json`, rewrites `stacklit.html` and opens it. It does not rescan the source, so run `generate` first if the code changed.

The HTML is one self-contained file with four views:

- **Graph**: force-directed dependency map. Click a node for exports, types and files.
- **Tree**: collapsible directory hierarchy with file and line counts.
- **Table**: sortable module table with search.
- **Flow**: top-down dependency flow from entrypoints to leaves.

A Share button downloads a standalone copy.

### stacklit diff

```
stacklit diff
```

Recomputes a content hash (Merkle hash) of the current source files and compares it with the `merkle_hash` stored in `stacklit.json`. It prints either "Index is up to date" or tells you to run `generate`. It exits with status 0 in both cases, so scripts should compare the output text or use the GitHub Action's check mode. Requires an index that has a `merkle_hash` field.

### stacklit derive

```
stacklit derive [--inject claude|cursor|aider]
```

Prints a compact navigation map built from `stacklit.json`: one header line, an entry and test line, one line per module with its purpose and key dependencies, hot files, the add-feature hint and do-not-touch paths. Size grows with the number of modules: 122 tokens for a 6-module Go repo, 1,122 for a 72-module TypeScript repo (see [bench/RESULTS.md](../bench/RESULTS.md)).

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--inject TARGET` | Insert or replace the map, between marker comments, in `CLAUDE.md` (`claude`), `.cursorrules` (`cursor`) or `.aider.conf.yml` (`aider`). The file is created if missing. Re-running replaces the previous block. |

### stacklit export

```
stacklit export [--format md] [--source FILE] [-o FILE]
```

Renders the index as markdown for people: a PR description, an issue, a chat message.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `--format` | `md` | `md`, or a graph format: `graphml`, `cypher`, `json`, `dot`, `mermaid`, `obsidian`, `markdown-wiki` |
| `--scope` | auto | Graph scope for single-file graph formats: `modules` or `symbols`. Auto picks symbols when `stacklit.graph.json` exists. |
| `--graph` | `stacklit.graph.json` | Symbol graph file for graph formats |
| `--budget` | 2000 | Token budget per `markdown-wiki` page. Env: `STACKLIT_EXPORT_PAGE_TOKENS`. |
| `--source` | `stacklit.json` | Index file to read |
| `-o`, `--output` | stdout | Write to this file (one-file formats) or directory (`obsidian`, `markdown-wiki`) instead |

The markdown contains the project title and totals, a language and framework table, entrypoints and key directories, a modules table, collapsible per-module export lists, the dependency edges with most-depended and isolated modules, hot files when git data exists, and the hints. Output is deterministic: the same `stacklit.json` always gives byte-identical markdown.

#### Graph formats

Graph formats print to stdout unless you pass `-o`, and never write into the repo on their own. Every node carries `source_file`, and symbol edges carry their confidence (`EXTRACTED`, `INFERRED` or `EXACT`) and score.

| Format | Output |
|--------|--------|
| `graphml` | One GraphML file (Gephi, yEd, NetworkX) |
| `cypher` | `CREATE` and `MATCH ... CREATE` statements for Neo4j and compatible stores |
| `json` | `{scope, nodes, edges}` |
| `dot` | Graphviz. Inferred edges are dashed. Capped to the highest-degree nodes (`STACKLIT_EXPORT_MAX_NODES`, default 300). |
| `mermaid` | Mermaid flowchart with the same cap |
| `obsidian` | A vault folder: `Index.md` plus one note per module with `[[wikilinks]]` to dependencies, and symbol headings that other notes link to as `[[module#Symbol]]` |
| `markdown-wiki` | `index.md` plus `modules/<module>.md`, each page cut off at the token budget with a "... N more" line. Same input gives identical files. |

```
stacklit export --format graphml -o /tmp/graph.graphml
stacklit export --format obsidian -o ~/vault/myproject
stacklit export --format markdown-wiki --budget 1500 -o /tmp/wiki
```

### stacklit setup

```
stacklit setup [claude|cursor|aider]
```

Uses the existing `stacklit.json`, or generates one if none exists, then configures AI tools:

| Target | Detected by | What it changes |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| `claude` | `claude` on PATH or a `CLAUDE.md` file | injects the map into `CLAUDE.md`, adds the stacklit server to `.mcp.json` |
| `cursor` | a `.cursor` directory or `.cursorrules` | injects the map into `.cursorrules`, adds `.cursor/mcp.json` |
| `aider` | `aider` on PATH or `.aider.conf.yml` | injects the map into `.aider.conf.yml` |

With no argument it configures every detected tool and installs the post-commit hook. If no tool is detected it prints the map to stdout so you can paste it. `.mcp.json` is listed in this repository's `.gitignore` because it is user-specific; decide for your own repo whether to commit it.

Claude Code crawl guard (opt in): `stacklit setup claude --crawl-guard[=nudge|redirect|off]` installs a `PreToolUse` hook that recognises repo-wide crawls (`find .`, `ls -R`, `tree`, `grep -r` or `rg` on the root, `Glob **/*`, a Read of a directory, generic "explore the codebase" subagent prompts). A bare `--crawl-guard` means `nudge`; pass a mode with `=`. `nudge` adds a pointer to the stacklit command. `redirect` denies with a reason naming the command, at most twice in a row per session and only while the index is current. `off` removes the hook, as does `--uninstall`. Supports `--dry-run`. Details in [docs/SESSIONS.md](SESSIONS.md#crawl-guard).

### stacklit guide

```
stacklit guide [--json]
```

Prints the agent usage guide (rules, command list, examples). It is the same text the strict rules block (steering `d`) uses, so you can paste it into any tool.

### stacklit refresh, digest and stats

Session plumbing, see [docs/SESSIONS.md](docs/SESSIONS.md) for the design.

```
stacklit refresh --files a.go,b.go [--json]    # or: --stdin with a hook payload
stacklit digest [--check] [--session ID]
stacklit stats [--json] [--since 7d]
```

- `refresh` updates `stacklit.json` (and `stacklit.graph.json` when it exists) for just the named files. Unchanged files are skipped by content hash, concurrent callers coalesce behind a lock, and writes are atomic. The result matches a full `generate`.
- `digest` prints the structure hash (module names, edges and exported names only). `--check` exits 0 when it equals what a session was given, 1 when it changed, 2 when nothing was recorded.
- `stats` reports the opt-in local usage log (`STACKLIT_STATS=1`). `served` is measured (bytes/4); `replaced_est` is an estimate of whole-file read cost, not a measured saving.

Claude Code hooks (opt-in, written to `.claude/settings.json`, or `~/.claude` with `--global`):

| Flag | Installs |
|---|---|
| `--session-hook` | `SessionStart` for startup, resume, clear and compact; `SubagentStart` for Explore and Plan |
| `--refresh-hook` | async `PostToolUse` on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit |

### stacklit serve

```
stacklit serve
```

Starts the MCP server on stdio. Run it from the repo root: it reads `stacklit.json` from the working directory. See [MCP server](#mcp-server).

### Symbol graph commands

```
stacklit graph                          # build stacklit.graph.json (query commands build it in memory if it is missing)
stacklit query "where is auth checked?" # scoped subgraph for a question, hard limit via --budget (default 2000 tokens)
stacklit explain <symbol>               # definition, location, callers, callees (--budget, default 1500)
stacklit impact <symbol|file>           # everything that depends on it (--depth, default 4)
stacklit path <from> <to>               # shortest path between two symbols
stacklit hubs -n 15                     # most connected symbols
stacklit communities                    # deterministic file clusters with labels
stacklit report -o GRAPH_REPORT.md      # key concepts, surprising links, suggested questions
stacklit slice <symbol>                 # only that symbol's source, with line numbers
stacklit watch                          # keep the graph current as files change
```

`query` prints files in relevance order: each file group is numbered (`1. path`) by the best score among its symbols (ties by path), symbols inside a file go by score then line, and a `best match: <file>:<line> <symbol>` line names the top result. Output is byte-stable between runs, and the `--budget` limit drops the lowest ranked results first. `--order relevance|path` picks the layout; `path` is the older alphabetical grouping with no numbers (default from `STACKLIT_QUERY_ORDER`, otherwise `relevance`). With `--json` each file has `rank` (1 is best) and `score` (0 to about 1.2, relative to the best seed), each symbol has its own `score`, and files stay in the printed order. The MCP `query_graph` and `query` tools return the same text. Two scoring knobs: `STACKLIT_AUX_PENALTY` (default 0.6) multiplies the score of files under test, example, benchmark or fixture directories unless the question mentions them (1 turns it off), and `STACKLIT_IDENT_TOKEN_BOOST` (default 0.5) raises symbols named exactly like a camelCase or snake_case word in the question.

All of them accept `--root`, `--graph`, `--include-tests` (keep test files in the graph; also `STACKLIT_GRAPH_INCLUDE_TESTS=1`) and (except `watch`) `--json`. Twenty languages produce symbols and call, import and inheritance edges; the per-language table is in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#symbol-graph-extraction). `STACKLIT_GRAPH_MAX_PARSE_BYTES` (default 196608) sets the largest file parsed with tree-sitter, and `STACKLIT_PARSE_MEMORY_MB` bounds concurrent parse memory. `watch` uses fsnotify and falls back to polling above `STACKLIT_WATCH_MAX` directories (default 4096); `STACKLIT_WATCH_POLL_MS` sets the polling interval.

### stacklit doctor

```
stacklit doctor [path] [--json] [--strict]
```

Checks the config file, git hook, index freshness and parse errors. `--strict` also fails on warnings.

### stacklit ingest

```
stacklit ingest [--docs] [--api] [--schema] [--owners] [--git-owners]
```

Writes `stacklit.context.json` next to the index and leaves `stacklit.json` untouched. With no connector flag, all but `--git-owners` run. Limits: `STACKLIT_INGEST_MAX_BYTES`, `STACKLIT_INGEST_MAX_ITEMS`.

#### Adapters

```
stacklit ingest --adapter "<command>" [--adapter-name NAME] [--adapter-files GLOBS] [--into-graph]
```

Runs your command with file paths on stdin (one per line, relative to the root) and reads JSON Lines back: `{"type":"node","id","name","kind","summary","source_file"}` and `{"type":"edge","from","to","kind"}`. Use it for concepts from PDFs, images, audio or anything else stacklit does not parse. Results are stored in `stacklit.context.json` as `concepts` and `concept_links`, always tagged `INFERRED` with a `source` field, and a rerun replaces that adapter's earlier output. `--into-graph` also adds them to `stacklit.graph.json` as `concept` nodes. Stacklit makes no network or model calls itself. Limits: `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_SEC` (60), `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_BYTES` (4 MiB), `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_ITEMS` (5000). The full contract and an example are in [examples/adapters](../examples/adapters/README.md).

#### SCIP

```
stacklit ingest --scip index.scip [--graph stacklit.graph.json]
```

Reads a SCIP index (from `scip-go`, `scip-typescript` and similar) with a built-in decoder and upgrades `INFERRED` graph edges to `EXACT` where the index shows a reference from the edge's source to a symbol defined at its target. It never adds or removes edges and rewrites the graph file in place. Size cap: `STACKLIT_SCIP_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB).

### stacklit check

```
stacklit check [--root DIR] [--source stacklit.json] [--json]
```

Evaluates the `check` block of `.stacklitrc.json` against the module graph. Exit code 3 when any rule is violated, 0 otherwise, so it works as a CI step.

```json
{
  "check": {
    "forbidden": [{ "from": "ui/**", "to": "core/db", "reason": "go through the service layer" }],
    "cycles": true,
    "max_fan_in": 12,
    "max_fan_out": 8,
    "orphans": true
  }
}
```

Patterns are module paths with `*` wildcards; `dir/**` matches `dir` and everything below it. With no `check` block the command passes. `--json` prints `{ok, violations:[{rule, message, modules}]}`.

### stacklit merge-graphs

```
stacklit merge-graphs a/stacklit.graph.json b/stacklit.graph.json -o merged.json [--multi stacklit-multi.json]
```

Combines symbol graphs from several repos. Node IDs get a `repo:` prefix, each node keeps its `source_file` and gets a `repo` field. Name a repo explicitly with `name=path.json`. With `--multi` (the output of `generate --multi`), repo nodes and `depends_on` edges are added for repos that depend on each other through manifest package names, plus import edges from the importing files to the provider repo.

---

## MCP server

```bash
stacklit serve
```

Fifteen read-only tools. The first seven read `stacklit.json`; the last eight read the symbol graph (`stacklit.graph.json`, built in memory when missing).

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|------|-------|---------|
| `get_overview` | none | project name and type, languages, frameworks, entrypoints, file and line totals |
| `get_module` | `name` (exact module name) | one module: purpose, exports, types, dependencies, files, activity |
| `find_module` | `query` (substring) | up to 5 modules whose name or purpose contains the query, case-insensitive. It does not search exports or file names. |
| `list_modules` | none | every module with purpose, file and line counts, activity, sorted by name |
| `get_dependencies` | `module` | the dependency edges that touch that module |
| `get_hot_files` | none | the most-changed files in the last 90 days |
| `get_hints` | none | add-feature guidance, test command, env var names, do-not-touch paths |
| `query_graph` | `query`, optional `budget` | scoped symbol subgraph grouped by file, hard token budget (default 2000) |
| `shortest_path` | `from`, `to` | shortest path between two symbols with weakest-hop confidence |
| `explain_symbol` | `symbol` | definition, file and line range, signature, callers and callees |
| `impact` | `symbol` (name, `Type.Method` or file path), optional `depth`, `budget` | symbols and files that depend on it |
| `get_hubs` | optional `top` | most connected symbols |
| `get_communities` | none | deterministic file clusters with labels |
| `graph_report` | none | key concepts, surprising links, suggested questions |
| `slice_symbol` | `symbol` | only that symbol's source lines |

The server re-reads `stacklit.json` whenever its modification time changes, so you do not need to restart it after `generate`.

---

## Configuration

Create `.stacklitrc.json` in the project root. The file is optional and every key is optional.

```json
{
  "ignore": ["vendor/", "generated/", "*.pb.go"],
  "max_depth": 3,
  "max_modules": 150,
  "max_exports": 15,
  "output": {
    "json": "stacklit.json",
    "mermaid": "DEPENDENCIES.md",
    "html": "stacklit.html"
  }
}
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `ignore` | none | Extra gitignore-style patterns to skip, on top of `.gitignore` and the built-in skips (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `.venv`, `__pycache__` and similar) |
| `max_depth` | 4 | How deep module detection goes in the directory tree |
| `max_modules` | 200 | Above this many modules, deeper ones are collapsed into their parents |
| `max_exports` | 10 | Exports kept per module, taken from the files with the most exports first. Symbols beyond the cap are not in the index, so raise it if lookups by symbol name miss. Env: `STACKLIT_MAX_EXPORTS`. |
| `max_module_files` | 30 | File names listed per module, files with the most exports first. Env: `STACKLIT_MAX_MODULE_FILES`. |
| `module_split_files` | 40 | A module with more files than this is split by subdirectory, repeatedly, so one big directory does not hide its files. Env: `STACKLIT_MODULE_SPLIT_FILES` (`-1` turns splitting off). |
| `output.json`, `output.mermaid`, `output.html` | `stacklit.json`, `DEPENDENCIES.md`, `stacklit.html` | Output file names. The outputs are excluded from the next scan automatically. |
| `timestamps` | false | Write `generated_at`. Off by default so a committed index only changes when the code does. Env: `STACKLIT_TIMESTAMPS=1`. |
| `git_activity` | false | Add git hot and recent files to the index. Off by default for the same reason; opt in with this key or `STACKLIT_GIT=1`. |
| `steering` | `a` | Wording of the rules at the top of the generated `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` block: `a`, `b`, `c` or `d` (see [docs/SESSIONS.md](docs/SESSIONS.md)). Env: `STACKLIT_STEERING`. |
| `crawl_guard` | (installed mode) | Crawl guard mode: `off`, `nudge` or `redirect`. Env: `STACKLIT_CRAWL_GUARD`. |
| `stats` | false | Append a local usage log of `query`, `slice`, `explain` and `impact` calls. Env: `STACKLIT_STATS=1`. Never networked. |
| `map_icons` | remote | `remote` lets the HTML map request language logos from thesvg.org when you open it. `off` removes every remote URL and shows letters instead. Env: `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off`. |
| `cache` | true | On-disk parse cache. `STACKLIT_NO_CACHE=1` disables it. |
| `workers` | CPU count | Parser pool size. Env: `STACKLIT_WORKERS`. |
| `parse_memory_mb` | 256 | Soft cap on the estimated memory of concurrent tree-sitter parses. A single file above the cap still parses, alone. Env: `STACKLIT_PARSE_MEMORY_MB` (0 disables the cap). |
| `parse_timeout_ms` | 3000 | Wall-clock budget per file for tree-sitter. A file that exceeds it is indexed with line count only and listed in `scan.lightweight`. Env: `STACKLIT_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MS` (0 disables). |
| `ts_max_bytes` | 131072 | Files larger than this skip tree-sitter (reason `large`). Env: `STACKLIT_TS_MAX_BYTES` (0 disables). |
| `max_line_len` | 2000 | A line longer than this marks the file minified and skips tree-sitter. Env: `STACKLIT_MAX_LINE_LEN` (0 disables). |
| `skip_generated` | true | Files named `.min.`, `.pb.`, `.gen.` or marked "generated" / "do not edit" in the first KB skip tree-sitter. Env: `STACKLIT_SKIP_GENERATED`. |
| `memory_limit_mb` | 448 | Soft Go heap limit during a scan, to keep RSS near the live set. An explicit `GOMEMLIMIT` wins. Env: `STACKLIT_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB` (0 disables). |

Diagnostics: `STACKLIT_TRACE=1` prints files whose parse took over 250 ms; `STACKLIT_PPROF=<dir>` writes `cpu.pprof`, `heap.pprof` and `heap-peak.pprof`.

| `check` | none | Architecture rules for `stacklit check`: `forbidden`, `cycles`, `max_fan_in`, `max_fan_out`, `orphans` (see [stacklit check](#stacklit-check)) |

A file that is missing, unreadable or invalid JSON is ignored and the defaults are used.

Only files with recognised source extensions are scanned. Directories named `test`, `tests`, `testdata`, `fixtures`, `e2e`, `bench` or `benchmarks` are left out of the module list, and each module lists up to about 20 file names.

---

## Environment variables

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD` | `init --summary` | Command (split on whitespace) that reads a prompt on stdin and prints the summary. Default: `claude -p`. |
| `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT` | `init --summary` | Timeout in seconds. Default: 120. |
| `STACKLIT_EXPORT_PAGE_TOKENS` | `export --format markdown-wiki`, `obsidian` | Token budget per page. Default: 2000. |
| `STACKLIT_EXPORT_MAX_NODES` | `export --format dot`, `mermaid` | Node cap, highest degree kept. Default: 300. |
| `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_SEC`, `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_BYTES`, `STACKLIT_ADAPTER_MAX_ITEMS` | `ingest --adapter` | Adapter timeout, output size and item caps. Defaults: 60, 4194304, 5000. |
| `STACKLIT_DIGEST_TOKENS` | `setup`, hooks | Token cap of the injected digest. Default 200. |
| `STACKLIT_STEERING` | `setup` | Steering wording variant `a`, `b`, `c` or `d`. |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_GUARD` | `hook crawl` | `off`, `nudge` or `redirect`. Overrides the `crawl_guard` config key and the mode the hook was installed with. Default off when nothing sets it. |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_REDIRECTS`, `STACKLIT_CRAWL_FRESH_TTL` | `hook crawl` | Consecutive redirects per session before the guard stands down (default 2), and seconds a staleness verdict is reused (default 10). |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_MAX_DEPTH`, `STACKLIT_CRAWL_PROMPT_CHARS` | `hook crawl` | Deepest `find -maxdepth` or `tree -L` still treated as narrow (default 1), and longest subagent prompt judged generic (default 600). |
| `STACKLIT_CRAWL_POINTER_MAX_BYTES`, `STACKLIT_CRAWL_STATE_DAYS` | `hook crawl` | Largest graph loaded to build an exact pointer (default 8 MiB), and days before session state files are pruned (default 7). |
| `STACKLIT_STATS` | `query`, `slice`, `explain`, `impact` | `1` logs usage locally, `0` forces it off. |
| `STACKLIT_CACHE_DIR` | cache, hooks, stats | Where the parse cache, session state and usage log live. |
| `STACKLIT_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS`, `STACKLIT_LOCK_STALE_SEC` | `refresh` | Debounce before a refresh (default 30) and age at which a lock is treated as abandoned (default 30). |
| `STACKLIT_SUBAGENT_TYPES` | `hook subagent` | Comma list of agent types that get the digest. Default `Explore,Plan`. |
| `STACKLIT_SCIP_MAX_BYTES` | `ingest --scip` | Largest SCIP file read. Default: 512 MiB. |

### Summary (opt-in)

`stacklit init --summary` runs the command above with a prompt made of a short instruction plus a JSON snapshot of the index (project, tech, modules with exports and dependencies, entrypoints). No file contents are included. The output is stored under `architecture.ai_summary` in `stacklit.json`. If the command fails, a warning is printed and the index is written without a summary. Stacklit itself opens no network connection; whether the command you configure does is up to that command.

---

## Reading stacklit.json

### Project and tech

```json
{
  "project": { "name": "my-app", "type": "monorepo" },
  "tech": {
    "primary_language": "typescript",
    "languages": { "typescript": { "files": 120, "lines": 14000 } },
    "frameworks": ["React", "Express"]
  },
  "structure": {
    "entrypoints": ["src/index.ts"],
    "total_files": 120,
    "total_lines": 14000
  }
}
```

`tech.framework_patterns` adds detected routes, API, middleware and entry locations for known frameworks. `merkle_hash` is the content hash used by `stacklit diff` and the git hook to skip needless regeneration.

### Modules

Each module is a directory of related source files:

```json
"src/auth": {
  "purpose": "Authentication and authorization",
  "language": "typescript",
  "files": 8,
  "lines": 1200,
  "file_list": ["service.ts", "middleware.ts", "types.ts"],
  "exports": ["AuthProvider", "useSession()", "loginAction(email, password)"],
  "type_defs": { "AuthState": "user User, token string, isLoading boolean" },
  "depends_on": ["src/db", "src/config"],
  "depended_by": ["src/api", "src/middleware"],
  "activity": "high"
}
```

- **purpose**: derived from the directory name and a built-in vocabulary, so it is generic (for example "Json" for a `json` directory). It is not a semantic summary.
- **exports**: public functions, classes and types with signatures where the language provides them, capped by `max_exports`.
- **type_defs**: field definitions of key structs, interfaces and classes.
- **depends_on / depended_by**: module-level graph built from import statements. Entries are sometimes shortened to the last path segment.
- **activity**: `high`, `medium` or `low` from 90-day git commit frequency.

### Dependencies

```json
"dependencies": {
  "edges": [["src/api", "src/auth"], ["src/auth", "src/db"]],
  "most_depended": ["src/db", "src/config"],
  "isolated": ["scripts"]
}
```

`most_depended` ranks modules by number of dependents. `isolated` lists modules with no edges in or out.

### Git and hints

```json
"git": { "hot_files": [{ "path": "src/api/routes.ts", "commits_90d": 14 }] },
"hints": {
  "add_feature": "Add handler in src/api, register in src/index.ts",
  "test_command": "npm test",
  "env_vars": ["DATABASE_URL", "JWT_SECRET"],
  "do_not_touch": ["migrations/", ".github/"]
}
```

`env_vars` holds names found in `os.Getenv`, `process.env` and `os.environ` style accesses. Values are never read. Hints are heuristics: the test command comes from well-known build files and the add-feature hint from module names such as `api` or `handler`.

---

## Monorepo support

Workspaces are detected automatically and appear as module groups in the index.

| Tool | Detection |
|------|-----------|
| pnpm | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` |
| npm, yarn | `package.json` `workspaces` field |
| Go | `go.work` |
| Turborepo | `turbo.json` |
| Nx | `nx.json` |
| Lerna | `lerna.json` |
| Cargo | `Cargo.toml` `[workspace]` section |
| Convention | `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`, `libs/` directories |

---

## Polyrepo scanning

Scan several separate repositories at once:

```bash
echo "/path/to/repo-a" > repos.txt
echo "/path/to/repo-b" >> repos.txt
stacklit init --multi repos.txt
```

Blank lines and `#` comments in the file are skipped. The result is `stacklit-multi.json` in the current directory, with module data for each repo and combined totals. Cross-repo dependency edges are not computed; that is on the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).

---

## CI/CD

### GitHub Action

[glincker/stacklit-action](https://github.com/glincker/stacklit-action) keeps the index fresh:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: glincker/stacklit-action@v1            # auto-commit (default)
# or: with: { mode: check }                   # fail the PR if the index is stale
```

Give the job `permissions: contents: write` in auto-commit mode.

### Hand-written workflow

```yaml
name: Update stacklit index
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore: ['stacklit.json', 'DEPENDENCIES.md', '**.md']

jobs:
  stacklit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.25'
      - run: go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest
      - run: stacklit generate --quiet
      - uses: stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@v5
        with:
          commit_message: "chore: update stacklit index"
          file_pattern: "stacklit.json DEPENDENCIES.md"
```

### Git hook

```bash
stacklit init --hook     # or: stacklit setup
```

Runs `stacklit generate --quiet` after each commit and stages the two committed outputs for the next commit.

---

## Troubleshooting

**The session hook does not fire, the index looks stale, or two sessions collide**: see the troubleshooting section of [docs/SESSIONS.md](docs/SESSIONS.md). Quick checks: `/hooks` in Claude Code, `echo '{"source":"startup","cwd":"'$PWD'"}' | stacklit hook session`, `stacklit status`, and `stacklit refresh --files <paths>`.

**`could not read stacklit.json`**: run `stacklit init` or `stacklit generate` first, and run the command from the repo root.

**A symbol is missing from the index**: exports are capped per module. Raise `max_exports` in `.stacklitrc.json` and regenerate. Unexported (private) symbols are never listed.

**A dependency looks wrong**: the graph comes from import statements resolved to modules. Test files and relative imports can produce extra or missing edges. Confirm with a read, and open an issue with a minimal example.

**Generation is slow or uses a lot of memory on Python or TypeScript**: this is a known cost of the pure-Go tree-sitter parsers. Add large generated or vendored directories to `ignore`.

**Windows install problems**: use `go install`, or download the binary from Releases and put it on your PATH.


---

<!-- source: docs/INSTALL.md -->

# Install

Every way to get Stacklit, with the exact command. Paths marked "after" are not live yet; the status column says what they wait for.

## Quick pick

| Path | Command | Gives you | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npx | `npx stacklit init` | CLI, one run, no install | live |
| npm global | `npm install -g stacklit` | CLI | live |
| Homebrew | `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit` | CLI | live |
| go install | `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest` | CLI | live |
| install.sh | see below | CLI, checksum verified | live once this file is on the default branch |
| Release archive | download from GitHub Releases | CLI | live |
| Docker | `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/glincker/stacklit init` | CLI in a container | after the image is published (see below) |
| Claude Code plugin | two commands below | hooks, skill and MCP server | live once this file is on the default branch |
| MCP registry | `io.github.glincker/stacklit` | MCP server entry for registry-aware clients | after the next npm release and a registry publish |
| skills.sh | `npx skills add glincker/stacklit` | the skill only | should work from the GitHub repo; listing on skills.sh is unverified |

What each one gives:

| | CLI | Hooks | Skill | MCP server |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npx, npm, brew, go install, install.sh, archive, Docker | yes | via `stacklit setup` | via `stacklit setup` | via `stacklit setup` |
| Claude Code plugin | needs the CLI on PATH | yes | yes | yes (minimal profile) |
| MCP registry | needs npm or the CLI | no | no | yes |
| skills.sh | no | no | yes | no |

## Command line

```bash
npx stacklit init                 # no install
npm install -g stacklit
brew install glincker/tap/stacklit
go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest
```

Then, in your repo:

```bash
stacklit init
```

## install.sh

Detects OS and architecture (Linux and macOS, amd64 and arm64), downloads the release archive and `checksums.txt`, verifies the sha256 and installs to `~/.local/bin` without sudo.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/stacklit/master/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

Options go after `sh -s --`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/stacklit/master/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version 0.5.0 --prefix /usr/local
```

`--dry-run` downloads and verifies but installs nothing. If you would rather read it first, open `scripts/install.sh`; it is short. Windows is not supported by the script: use npm or the zip from Releases.

## Docker

The repository has a multi-stage `docker/Dockerfile` (distroless final image, entrypoint `stacklit`). Build it yourself:

```bash
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t stacklit .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work stacklit init
```

Once the image is published to ghcr.io, the same works without building:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/glincker/stacklit init
```

On Linux, add `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` so generated files belong to you. The image has no shell and no git binary, so features that call git (hot files, the post-commit hook installer) do not work in it. Use the native binary for those. The MCP server over Docker (`docker run -i --rm -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/glincker/stacklit serve`) works for the index tools.

## Claude Code plugin

The repo is a Claude Code plugin marketplace. It needs the `stacklit` binary on PATH (any CLI path above).

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add glincker/stacklit
claude plugin install stacklit@stacklit
```

Inside a session the same are `/plugin marketplace add glincker/stacklit` and `/plugin install stacklit@stacklit`.

The plugin adds:

- the Stacklit skill
- a SessionStart hook (`stacklit hook session`) that injects the map
- an async PostToolUse hook (`stacklit hook posttool`) that refreshes the map for edited files
- an MCP server running `stacklit serve --profile minimal`

Both hooks exit quietly if `stacklit` is not installed. The crawl guard is not included; enable it with `stacklit setup claude --crawl-guard`. The hook wrapper uses `sh`, so on Windows it needs Git Bash.

## MCP registry

`server.json` at the repo root describes the server for the official MCP registry under the name `io.github.glincker/stacklit`. It points at the npm package, which declares the same name in `mcpName`. That field ships with the first npm release after it was added, and the registry entry is published by the maintainers after that. Until then, use `stacklit setup` or the plugin to wire the MCP server.

## Skill only

```bash
npx skills add glincker/stacklit
```

This installs `skills/stacklit/SKILL.md` into the agents it detects. The skill follows the open Agent Skills format.

## Not available yet

Scoop, WinGet, Nix, AUR, mise and a devcontainer feature are not published. Windows users can use `npm install -g stacklit` or the zip from Releases.


---

<!-- source: docs/LANGUAGES.md -->

# Languages

Stacklit indexes 48 languages and formats. Each row shows what is extracted. Any other language gets line counts and language detection only.

| Language | Extracts |
|----------|----------|
| Go | imports, exports with signatures, struct fields, interface methods |
| TypeScript/JS | imports (ESM, CJS, dynamic), classes, interfaces, type aliases |
| Python | imports, classes with methods, type hints, decorators |
| Rust | use/mod/crate, pub items with generics, trait methods |
| Java | imports, public classes, method signatures with types |
| C# | using directives, public types, method signatures |
| Ruby | require, classes, modules, methods |
| PHP | namespace use, classes, traits, public methods |
| Kotlin | imports, classes, objects, enum entries, functions with signatures |
| Swift | imports, structs, classes, protocols |
| C/C++ | includes, non-static functions, structs, unions, enums, classes, typedefs, namespaces |
| Elixir | alias/import/require/use, modules, protocols, public def/defmacro, structs, @type/@callback |
| Zig | @import, pub functions, pub structs/enums/unions with methods, pub constants |
| Dart | imports/exports, classes, mixins, enums, extensions, typedefs, public functions and methods |
| Scala | imports (with selectors), traits, classes, objects, enums, type aliases, defs and vals |
| Lua | require, non-local functions, `M.fn` and `M:method` definitions |
| Shell | source/`.` includes, function definitions |
| SQL | tables with columns, views, functions |
| GDScript | class_name, signals, constants, enums, public funcs, inner classes, preload/load paths |
| Vue / Svelte | script block imports, exports, types (parsed as TypeScript) |
| Terraform/HCL | resources, data sources, variables, outputs, modules, providers, module sources |
| Protobuf | imports, messages (nested), enums, services with rpc signatures |
| Haskell | imports, signatures (honors the module export list), data/newtype/class declarations |
| OCaml | open/include, let bindings, types with constructors and fields, modules, exceptions |
| Clojure | ns requires/imports, `defn`/`def`/`defmacro`, protocols and records |
| R | library/require/source, non-dot functions with parameters, top-level constants |
| Perl | use/require/parent, packages, public subs |
| Julia | using/import, exported functions, structs, abstract types, constants |
| Objective-C | #import, `@interface`, `@protocol`, methods and properties |
| Groovy | imports, classes, interfaces, enums, top-level `def` functions |
| Nim | imports, star-exported procs, funcs, types with fields, constants |
| Erlang | includes, exported functions as name/arity, records, types |
| F# | open, modules, types (unions, records, members), non-private lets |
| Fortran | use, modules, functions, subroutines, derived types |
| Elm | imports, exposed annotated values and types |
| Solidity | imports, contracts, interfaces, libraries, public functions, events, structs |
| PowerShell | Import-Module/using/dot-sourcing, functions with params, classes |
| Gleam | imports, pub functions, types with constructors, constants |
| CMake | include/add_subdirectory/find_package, project, library/executable/custom targets, functions, macros |
| Makefile | includes, explicit targets with prerequisites |
| Dockerfile | base images, build stages, exposed ports |
| YAML / TOML / JSON | top-level keys (capped, see below) |
| GraphQL | object/interface/enum/input/union/scalar types with fields, named operations and fragments |

Config files (YAML, TOML, JSON) report at most `STACKLIT_CONFIG_KEY_CAP` top-level keys (default 40) and skip key extraction above `STACKLIT_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES` (default 262144). Lockfiles and the generated `stacklit.json` are not indexed. Go is parsed with the Go standard library; every other row uses tree-sitter. SQL `$$` function bodies are masked before parsing so later statements still extract. Grammar-specific caveats: Groovy extraction falls back to line patterns where the grammar errors out, and `.m` files are treated as Objective-C.

Any other language gets basic support (line count + language detection).

The symbol graph (`stacklit graph`, `query`, `impact`, `slice`) covers 20 languages; the per-language table is in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#symbol-graph-extraction). The other languages still get the module index.

Monorepos are detected automatically: pnpm, npm and yarn workspaces, Go workspaces, Turborepo, Nx, Lerna, Cargo workspaces, and `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`, `libs/` conventions.


---

<!-- source: docs/FAQ.md -->

# FAQ

Short answers about what Stacklit reads, when it helps, how accurate its dependency edges are and how it fits with git and assistants.

**Does it read my code?**
Yes, locally, to extract structure with tree-sitter. Nothing leaves your machine unless you pass `--summary` (see Privacy).

**Does it help on small repos?**
Less. If the whole repo fits comfortably in a prompt, an agent can just read it. The index pays off once exploring costs more than reading a map, and it saves the most when the agent would otherwise read several large files to confirm a location.

**When is grep better?**
When you already know the exact identifier. A single grep is cheaper than loading a map. The index helps with questions grep cannot answer in one step, such as "what depends on this module" or "where would a new adapter go".

**How accurate are the dependency edges?**
Module-level edges are built from import statements and are good enough to orient an agent, but not exact. In the benchmark, 4 of 7 "what depends on X" lookups were fully correct. Known weak spots: test files counted as dependents, relative imports resolved to the wrong module, and short module names that can be ambiguous. Treat the graph as a guide and confirm with a read.

**What if my language is not supported?**
Files are still counted and language-detected, and the module map, git activity and hints still work. Exports and dependency edges need a parser.

**Does the git hook slow commits down?**
It runs `stacklit generate --quiet` after each commit. On Go repos of this size that is tens of milliseconds; on Python and TypeScript repos in the benchmark it took a few seconds. If that is too slow, run `stacklit generate` manually or in CI instead.

**Can I keep the Mermaid file out of the repo root?**
Yes. Set `"output": {"mermaid": "docs/DEPENDENCIES.md"}` in `.stacklitrc.json`. The git hook stages the configured path.

**Can I use it with Copilot?**
Yes. Commit `stacklit.json` and tell Copilot to read it in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or paste the output of `stacklit derive` there.

**How is it different from dumping the whole repo into a prompt?**
A dump is the full source. Stacklit is structure only: it is orders of magnitude smaller but cannot answer questions that need code bodies. See [COMPARISON.md](COMPARISON.md) for a factual feature comparison.


---

<!-- source: docs/PRIVACY.md -->

# Privacy

Stacklit runs locally. It reads your source files on your machine, writes its outputs into your repository, and makes no network requests of its own.

- No telemetry, no analytics, no account, no upload.
- The generated HTML map is one file with no scripts or fonts from anywhere. The only thing it fetches is small language logos: when you open it, it requests an icon file per language and framework (for example `https://thesvg.org/icons/go/default.svg`) from thesvg.org, with a copy on cdn.jsdelivr.net as a backup. The requests carry only the icon name, no repo data, cookies or referrer, and a Content-Security-Policy blocks every other request. The page works offline with letters in place of logos. Set `STACKLIT_MAP_ICONS=off` or `"map_icons": "off"` in `.stacklitrc.json` to leave no remote URL in the page.
- The only network activity in the whole project happens outside the program: `npx stacklit` and `npm install -g stacklit` download the release binary from GitHub when you install.
- The one opt-in exception is `stacklit init --summary`. It pipes a snapshot of the index (module names, exports, dependency edges, entrypoints; no file contents) to a command you control, `claude -p` by default or whatever `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD` names. Whether that command talks to a network is up to that command. Without the flag, nothing is sent anywhere.

`stacklit.json` lists names of modules, files and exported symbols, and detected environment variable names (not values). Review it before committing a private repo's index to a public place.


---

<!-- source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md -->

# Architecture

Stacklit is a single Go binary. It walks a repository, parses each source file into a small record of imports and exports, groups files into modules, resolves imports into module-level edges, and renders the result in several formats. There is no daemon, database or network client in the core path.

## Pipeline

`stacklit generate` (and `init`) run one pipeline, implemented in `internal/engine/engine.go`:

```
walk files -> parse each file -> build module graph -> git activity -> assemble index -> render outputs
```

| Step | Package | What it does |
|------|---------|--------------|
| Config | `internal/config` | Loads optional `.stacklitrc.json` over defaults (depth, module and export caps, ignore patterns, output names) |
| Monorepo detection | `internal/monorepo` | Detects pnpm, npm and yarn workspaces, `go.work`, Turborepo, Nx, Lerna, Cargo workspaces and convention directories |
| Walk | `internal/walker` | Lists indexable source files in sorted order. Honors `.gitignore`, config ignores and built-in skips (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, virtualenvs). Keeps only known source extensions. |
| Parse | `internal/parser` | Turns each file into a `FileInfo`: language, imports, exports with signatures, type definitions, line count, entrypoint flag |
| Graph | `internal/graph` | Groups files into modules by directory, resolves imports to modules, produces edges, most-depended and isolated lists |
| Detect | `internal/detect` | Frameworks (from imports and config files), framework patterns (routes, API, middleware, entry), environment variable names |
| Git | `internal/git` | 90-day commit counts per file (hot files), recent files, Merkle content hash, post-commit hook installer |
| Assemble | `internal/engine` | Builds the `schema.Index`, derives purpose strings, hints (add feature, test command, do-not-touch) |
| Summary (optional) | `internal/summary` | With `--summary`, runs a user-configured command on an index snapshot |
| Render | `internal/renderer` | `stacklit.json`, `DEPENDENCIES.md` (Mermaid), `stacklit.html`, markdown export |

Other consumers of the index:

| Package | Role |
|---------|------|
| `internal/derive` | Builds the compact navigation map and injects it between marker comments into agent config files |
| `internal/setup` | Detects Claude Code, Cursor and Aider and writes their config and MCP entries |
| `internal/mcp` | MCP server over stdio, backed by `stacklit.json` |
| `internal/cli` | Cobra commands that wire the above together |
| `internal/schema` | The `Index` types shared by every package |

## Parsers

`internal/parser/parser.go` keeps an ordered registry and uses the first parser whose `CanParse` accepts the file:

1. `GoParser` uses the standard library `go/parser`. It gives exact signatures and struct fields with no external dependency.
2. `TreeSitterParser` handles TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, JSX, Python, Rust, Java, C#, Ruby, PHP, Kotlin, Swift, C and C++. It uses a pure-Go tree-sitter runtime (no cgo), so the binary cross-compiles to every release target without a C toolchain. Each language has an extractor in `internal/parser/ts_*.go`.
3. `GenericParser` is the fallback. It records line count and language only.

Adding a language means adding an extractor and registering it in `tsLangMap`; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Modules and dependency resolution

A module is a directory. A file's module is its parent directory, collapsed to at most `max_depth` path segments; files at the repo root belong to `root`. Modules with a path segment named `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `testdata`, `fixtures`, `e2e`, `benchmarks`, `bench` or `docs_src` are left out of the graph. When the module count would exceed `max_modules`, deeper modules fold into their parents.

Edges are built from import statements: each import string is matched against the known module names, preferring the longest match. Relative imports are resolved against the importing file's directory; Python dot-style imports are normalized first; Go imports are matched on the module path. Anything that matches no module is treated as external and dropped.

This is deliberately approximate. It works from import text, not from a type-checked symbol graph, so it can miss dynamic imports or re-exports, and it can add edges that come from test files. [bench/RESULTS.md](../bench/RESULTS.md) measures how often the resulting "what depends on X" answers are exactly right.

## The index

`internal/schema` defines `stacklit.json`. Top-level sections: `project`, `tech`, `structure`, `modules`, `dependencies`, `git`, `hints`, `architecture` and `merkle_hash`. Field-by-field description: [USAGE.md](USAGE.md#reading-stacklitjson).

Determinism is a design goal: files are walked in sorted order, maps are written with stable key order, and paths are normalized to forward slashes. The same source tree should produce the same index on any OS, which is what makes it safe to commit and to diff.

## Symbol graph extraction

`internal/graph` turns source files into symbols (functions, methods, types) and edges between them. Go uses the standard library AST. Every other language goes through one shared tree-sitter driver (`ts_driver.go`) that walks the parse tree once and is configured by a small table per language (`ts_lang_core.go`, `ts_lang_more.go`): which node types define symbols, which are calls, how imports and base types are read. Each symbol carries start and end line, a one-line signature, the first sentence of its doc comment and its visibility.

Memory is bounded. Concurrent parses share a weighted gate (`STACKLIT_PARSE_MEMORY_MB`, default 512), and a file larger than `STACKLIT_GRAPH_MAX_PARSE_BYTES` (default 192 KiB) skips tree-sitter. Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Rust and Java then fall back to the older line scanner; other languages keep only their file node. The line scanner also takes over when a Python tree contradicts the file's indentation, because the grammar runtime can silently drop a block. Test files are skipped unless `--include-tests` or `STACKLIT_GRAPH_INCLUDE_TESTS=1` is set.

### Edge kinds by language

`def` means symbols with spans, signature, doc and visibility. `typed` means receiver types are inferred from annotated parameters, typed locals, typed fields or constructor assignments, so `repo.find()` links to `Repo.find` instead of every `find`.

| Language | def | calls | imports | inherits | implements | typed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Go | yes | yes | yes | embedding | structural (inferred) | yes |
| Python | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| TypeScript, JavaScript | yes | yes | yes (import, require, re-export) | yes | yes (TypeScript) | yes |
| Rust | yes | yes | yes (use, mod) | trait bounds | impl Trait for | yes |
| Java | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| C# | yes | yes | yes (using) | yes | by position and I-prefix | yes |
| Kotlin | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Swift | yes | yes | module imports | yes | by position | yes |
| PHP | yes | yes | yes (use) | yes | yes | yes |
| Ruby | yes | yes | yes (require, require_relative) | yes | include, extend | yes |
| C | yes | yes | yes (#include, header and source pair) | no | no | yes |
| C++ | yes | yes | yes (#include) | yes | no | yes |
| Scala | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Dart | yes | yes | yes | yes | with, implements | yes |
| Elixir | yes | yes | yes (alias, import, use, require) | no | no | no |
| Lua | yes | yes | yes (require) | no | no | no |
| Zig | yes | yes | yes (@import) | no | no | no |
| Haskell | yes | yes | yes | no | no | no |
| OCaml | yes | yes | yes (open, qualified paths) | no | no | no |
| Solidity | yes | yes | yes | yes | by I-prefix | yes |

Where a clause lists bases without saying which are classes (C#, Swift, Scala, Solidity), the first non-interface name is `inherits` and the rest, or any name shaped like `IName`, are `implements`.

### Call resolution and confidence

Resolution is one pass over hash maps built once, so cost grows linearly with references. A call is resolved in this order, and the first rule that matches wins:

1. Same file, including the enclosing type's own methods.
2. Names imported from a file in the repo, then the package or namespace of the file.
3. Wildcard and namespace imports, in sorted order so output is stable.
4. A typed receiver (`@Type`), then that type's ancestors, then (for `this`, `self`, `super`) the enclosing type and its ancestors.
5. A qualifier bound to an import (`mod.fn`, `Alias.method`).
6. Last resort, a name guess across the repo.

A receiver whose type is known but lives outside the repo (`String`, a library class) links to nothing, rather than to a project method with the same name.

| Score | Confidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.00 | EXTRACTED | Same-file definition, or a unique type in the same file |
| 0.95 | EXTRACTED | Imported name that resolves to one definition |
| 0.90 | EXTRACTED | Qualified through an import, a wildcard import, a typed receiver or `this` |
| 0.85 | EXTRACTED | Static call on a project type |
| 0.80 | EXTRACTED | Method found on an ancestor type, or a member of a bound module whose owner name differs |
| 0.60 | INFERRED | Base type found only by unique name |
| 0.55 | INFERRED | Unknown receiver, one method of that name in the repo |
| 0.50 | INFERRED | Unqualified name, one function of that name in the repo |
| 0.45 | INFERRED | Receiver type is in the repo but no method was found on it |
| 0.25 to 0.50 | INFERRED | Several candidates (at most four), the score is split by candidate count |
| 0.30 | INFERRED | Generic names such as `get` or `close` with an unknown receiver |

Prototype-only declarations (C and C++ headers) are dropped as call targets when a definition of the same name is also a candidate.

## Staleness detection

`ComputeMerkle` hashes the sorted list of source files and their contents into a single root hash, stored as `merkle_hash`. `stacklit diff` recomputes it and compares. It covers only indexed source files, so edits to docs or configs do not make the index look stale.

## Compact map and injection

`derive.CompactMap` prints one line per module (purpose, up to four dependencies, up to four dependents when it has three or more), plus header, hot files and hints. `InjectIntoFile` wraps that in start and end marker comments and replaces the block in place on re-runs, so agent config files stay clean across regenerations. The map grows with module count, which is why `max_modules` also bounds its size.

## MCP server

`internal/mcp` registers fifteen read-only tools (seven over the index, eight over the symbol graph) with the official Go MCP SDK and serves them over stdio. Each call loads `stacklit.json` from the working directory, caching it until the file's modification time changes.

## Network use

None in the core path. `internal/summary` only runs a local command (`claude -p` by default, or `STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD`) and only when `--summary` is passed. The repository also contains `internal/summary/ai.go`, a direct API client that no command currently calls. The HTML output embeds everything it needs and loads nothing remotely. The npm wrapper downloads the release binary from GitHub at install time.

## Release and CI

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `go vet`, `go test -race` and a build on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` with `.goreleaser.yml`: cross-compiled binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, plus npm publish with trusted publishing.
- `.github/workflows/stacklit-index.yml`: regenerates this repository's own index on pushes to the default branch.
- `action/action.yml`: a composite action that installs stacklit and runs `generate`.
- `npm/`: the `npx stacklit` wrapper that downloads the matching release binary.

## Benchmarks

`bench/` is a separate `package main` inside the same module. It shells out to the built `stacklit` binary and reads `stacklit.json` as generic JSON, so it does not import the internal packages and cannot affect the shipped binary.

<!-- source: skills/stacklit/SKILL.md -->

---
name: stacklit
description: Use the stacklit codebase map (stacklit.json) to locate code and check blast radius before grep or glob.
---

Read `stacklit.json` before broad searches.

1. Missing or stale: `stacklit generate`.
2. Find the module by `purpose`, then read only its `file_list`.
3. Before editing, check `depended_by` and `dependencies.most_depended`.
4. New code goes where `hints.add_feature` says; verify with `hints.test_command`.
5. Respect `hints.do_not_touch`.

MCP tools, if connected: `get_overview`, `find_module`, `get_module`, `get_dependencies`, `list_modules`, `get_hot_files`, `get_hints`.

Docs, APIs, schemas, owners: `stacklit ingest`, then read `stacklit.context.json`.
Index drift: `stacklit diff`.
